decision.summary: All evaluated rules are within their PASS thresholds.

results.label: Bases with quality >= Q30 (after preprocessing)
results.rationale: Q30 means an estimated base-call error rate of 1 in 1,000. A low Q30 fraction increases the number of sequencing errors carried into alignment and variant calling.

results.label: Mean base quality (after preprocessing)
results.explanation: 33.24 Phred meets the PASS threshold (>= 30 Phred).
results.rationale: The average Phred score summarises base-call confidence across all retained bases.

results.label: Residual adapter content (after preprocessing)
results.rationale: Adapter sequence left in reads does not originate from the sample and can cause mis-alignment and false variants. FastQC warns above 5 % and fails above 10 %.

results.label: Read retention after preprocessing
results.rationale: Shows the cost of cleaning: a large loss of reads can indicate a poor library or overly strict trimming parameters, and reduces usable depth.

results.label: Duplicate reads (sampled, after preprocessing)
results.rationale: High duplication can indicate PCR over-amplification or low library complexity. Expected to be high for amplicon, small-RNA and highly expressed RNA-seq libraries.

results.label: Undetermined bases (N)
results.rationale: N bases are positions the sequencer could not call; a high fraction indicates instrument or cluster problems.

results.label: GC distribution deviation from normal
results.rationale: A per-read GC distribution that departs from a normal shape can indicate contamination or a biased library (FastQC thresholds: warn 15 %, fail 30 %).

results.label: Reads remaining after preprocessing
results.explanation: 38,586 reads meets the PASS threshold (>= 10,000 reads).
results.rationale: Too few reads limit statistical power. Set this to the depth your experiment needs.
